title: sovereign-routing-ops-playbook-drafts
content:
Purpose:
This is a working ops playbook for enforcing sovereign routing and region pinning for Private deployments. It captures recommended enforcement signals, operator workflows, telemetry queries, sample routing configs, and an initial canary/rollout sequence for customer environments that require strict data locality.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments and the private control plane routing decisions we make on ingestion/service-to-model calls. Focused on region pinning, fallback behavior, audit trails, KMS boundary handling, and operator runbook steps.
- Non-goals: Changes to hosted API pricing or customer contract language, application-level data classification (left to customer).

Key definitions (operator shorthand):
- Pin: explicit customer-configured tag that binds a request route to a region/affinity (e.g., pin.region = eu-west-1).
- Hard-enforce: deny / reject requests that violate pin; used only for regulatory-critical customers after agreement.
- Soft-enforce: log + route to preferred region when available; alert if cross-region fallback used.

Enforcement signals (ordered by priority):
1) Request pin metadata (customer-configured route).
2) Customer declared residency in tenant profile (tenant.metadata.residency).
3) Source network egress region (VPC subnets / peering region).
4) Account billing region as fallback.

Routing decision algorithm (pseudocode):
- If pin.present and hard_enforce: if local capacity and model variant available => route to pinned region; else => return 451 + audit_event (policy_violation).
- If pin.present and soft_enforce: if pinned region capacity available => route; else => route locally but tag audit and notify on-call.
- If no pin: use smart routing policy (latency-first with residency-aware weight) and annotate response with routing.reason.

Sample routing-config snippet (operator editable):
# example format used by routing service
routes:
  - name: tenant-eu-prod
    match: tenant.id == "T-12345"
    pin: eu-west-1
    enforcement: soft
    fallbacks: [eu-west-1-burst, eu-central-1]

Operational checklist for a new customer requiring sovereignty:
1) Verify contract/regulatory notes with legal (link to contract item).
2) Confirm tenant.profile.residency value and set pin if requested.
3) Provision KMS key in customer region and verify access from control plane shim.
4) Ensure private control plane has no egress to non-approved regions (VPC routing review).
5) Create tenant routing entry and set enforcement level.
6) Start canary: route 1% traffic, observe 48h of traffic and logs, check latency, model accuracy regressions.
7) Ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over weekly intervals unless regressions.

Telemetry & alerting (critical queries):
- %requests_routed_outside_pin by tenant (breakdown by reason).
- avg_inference_latency__p95_by_region for pinned tenants.
- model_variant_fallback_rate (counts of fallback to different quant/variant).
- audit_event.policy_violation count and last 30d details.

Sample Grafana / logs queries (operator copy-paste):
- Logs: level=info AND tenant.id=T-12345 AND audit.tag=residency_fallback | sort by @timestamp desc | limit 100
- Metrics: sum(rate(requests_routed_outside_pin[1h])) by (tenant_id)

Fallback and graceful degradation patterns:
- When pinned region is degraded, prefer slow/queued routing within region (burst pool) over cross-region routing if SLA allows.
- If model variant not available in region, attempt to load quantized variant; if incompatible, trigger A/B fallback to a regional replica and tag for audit.
- For hard_enforce customers: issue an incident (SEV2) and present human escalation path to legal and customer success rather than auto-fallback.

Audit log requirements:
- Must include: tenant_id, request_id, pin_present, routed_region, enforcement_mode, operator_action (if manual override), KMS_key_id (if used), timestamp, reason_code.
- Retention: default 90 days for private deploys; 365 days for enterprise compliance tier.

Testing matrix (pre-rollout):
- Connectivity: VPC egress allowed/blocked tests to confirm no traffic leaves allowed regions.
- Load: simulate traffic with pinned model at expected 1x/3x production.
- Model fidelity: run small holdout evaluation to ensure model behaviour unchanged by local quantization.
- Chaos: kill regional serving pool and validate fallback aligns to configured enforcement policy.

Operator runbook snippets (common tasks):
- Manual route override (temporary emergency): add override route with ttl=2h and annotate ticket.
- Remove pin: ensure customer confirmation and sign-off, update tenant profile and audit.
- Emergency rollback: set enforcement=soft globally for tenant and trigger rollback playbook.

Open questions (needs product/LEGAL sign-off):
- Should soft-enforce traffic that crosses borders be billed differently or tagged for cost reconciliation?
- For hybrid on-prem + cloud customers, what's the canonical source of truth for "region"? (customer vs control-plane discovery)
- What is the acceptable SLO degradation threshold before triggering human escalation for sovereign tenants?

Action items (next 30 days):
- (Aisha) Draft SLA language for hard vs soft enforcement liability (due 2024-11-09).
- (Liam) Add metric and dashboard scaffold for requests_routed_outside_pin (due 2024-11-04).
- (Diego) Prototype routing-config validation script that rejects configs with implicit cross-region fallthroughs (due 2024-11-15).

Notes to self: this doc will be folded into a more formal runbook once we finalize enforcement semantics with legal. Keep examples concrete and include test snippets that SRE can run in staging.

References and links:
- Confluence policy draft (linked above)
- ENG-4721 ticket for telemetry work
- routing-config PR#89 (prototype rules kernel)

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call when residency alerts fire:
1) Acknowledge alert and tag incident with tenant id.
2) Check audit logs for last 30 minutes for routing.reason.
3) Verify capacity in pinned region and model shard health.
4) If hard_enforce violation -> escalate to legal and CS; do NOT auto-fallback.
5) If soft_enforce violation -> enable burst pool or increase capacity, notify customer and document event.

-- end of draft --
